bounded_statement: Within the four visible files of this case, the selected result computes the nest predation rate over only the 44 retained (clutch-initiated) boxes (9/44 = 0.204545) yet labels and asserts it as "the nest predation rate for the complete planned set of 60 nest boxes," the declared target of inference; the report itself states no amendment or approved deviation exists, so a retained-subset rate is demonstrably presented as a complete-domain rate.

counterevidence_considered.description: Strongest counterevidence considered: the report transparently discloses the screening step and both counts (44 retained, 16 removed) and prints the raw fraction "9 / 44", so an attentive reader could detect the mismatch and recompute a complete-domain rate. This mitigates concealment but does not negate the issue: the asserted claim itself, in both the selected result and the method statement, attributes the subset-denominator rate to the complete planned set of 60 boxes, which is the defining pattern of the issue class.
counterevidence_considered.observed_value: disclosure present, but claim scope still mislabeled

extensions.x-stage1-falsification-attempt: I attempted to falsify the demonstrated-issue verdict three ways. First, I checked whether the selected result could be legitimately read as a retained-subset claim: it cannot, because the sentence explicitly names "the complete planned set of 60 nest boxes" as the scope of the rate, and the method statement repeats that attribution. Second, I checked for any stated amendment, deviation, or exposure-based rationale (for example, treating only clutch-initiated boxes as at-risk under a redefined target) that could reconcile the 44-box denominator with the 60-box claim; the report explicitly states no amendment or approved deviation exists and reasserts the complete planned set as the target. Third, I recomputed all counts from inputs/data.csv to rule out the possibility that 44 was actually the planned count or that the labels were merely transposed; the data confirm 60 planned rows, 44 retained, and 9 events, so 9/44 is unambiguously the retained-subset rate presented under a complete-domain label. All three falsification routes failed.

root_cause: workflow/analysis.py sets the exposure denominator to the retained subset (denominator = n_retained, under a comment stating the denominator is "the retained post-screening subset only") while the report's templated claim text and method statement attribute the resulting rate to the complete planned set of all planned boxes, producing a scope label that contradicts the computed quantity.
